answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the nectar identifier and voids the later submissions, so that the operator forfeits for 361 runs and collects one. Because the lagoon index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the pearl audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 361 answers need 361 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
